1.tense: Strength is moving outward from you now, by measure, and it lands where it is needed.
1.verb: to share strength outward, in measure, with the people near you
1.place: in the open field before anything has been chosen
1.ask: Pick the season you want next and what it's for, then take a single step toward it that a friend would notice.
1.core:
You can hand strength to someone and still have enough left for your own day. What you pass along tends to land where it's needed, and people settle near you without knowing why. That's a real skill, and it isn't the same as being endlessly available.

Something is still unspent, though. You've kept your strength moving without deciding what the whole of it is for. Name the direction you actually want, not the one that keeps things smooth, and take one step in it this week. Not a plan. One step, where a friend would notice it happen. Strength that goes somewhere carries further than strength scattered in every direction at once.
1.sheetLine: You can give and still have enough.

2.tense: You will have handed your strength out past what you had, and you will still be looking for the next one who needs it.
2.verb: to share strength outward, in measure, with the people near you
2.place: in the open field before anything has been chosen
2.ask: Set who you're helping and what each cost beside what comes back to you, and see whether the two sides line up.
2.core:
You're spending ahead. Someone needs something and your hand is already open — money, hours, the strength to fix it — before you've checked whether it was yours to carry. From the outside this still looks like generosity. From the inside it's getting hard to tell where helping ends and bracing begins. When you've given past your own supply, the ones close to you start needing you to be fine, and nobody says so.

Giving less isn't the answer. Being honest about the ledger is. List who you're carrying and what it costs, beside what they carry for you. Two columns, no rounding in your own favour. Keep the page private. You'll see the shape of it in about a minute — where there's surplus, and where you've been paying quietly and calling it love.
2.sheetLine: You give until there's nothing left to give from.

3.tense: You were strong enough to carry things to people once, and the carrying stopped.
3.verb: to share strength outward, in measure, with the people near you
3.place: in the open field before anything has been chosen
3.ask: Think of somebody you still mean to stand by, and change how you reach them — a different contact, or a smaller one — even if the old way is what you know.
3.core:
You are not hard or stingy. Some form of giving got set down at a point you may not remember choosing, and being set down became the norm. The people who used to get your help have quietly stopped asking. A door you meant to walk back through is still behind you, and you haven't noticed that it's behind you.

You don't have to get big again. Pick somebody you still mean to stand by, and change the method — a shorter visit, a different kind of help, one thing instead of everything. The commitment stays; the way you meet it doesn't have to look like it used to. Small works here. What got interrupted wasn't your strength. It was the form you were doing it in.
3.sheetLine: The strength you were going to share stayed with you.

4.tense: You are already steering by a direction you chose, and it has not been named as yours.
4.verb: to share strength outward, in measure, with the people near you
4.place: in the open field before anything has been chosen
4.ask: Look at where your effort went this week, find the heading it kept, and say that heading was your choice.
4.core:
Something in your life has been turning toward a chosen direction and gathering weight, and it isn't filed under your name. You may be calling it circumstances, or how the month went, or what someone needed. It's been a heading the whole time. Support moves by measure, and you've been metering — choosing what gets your strength and what doesn't — while the deciding stayed off the record.

Stop surveying. More than one direction was open, and the one you keep returning to is the one. Say it plainly, in a sentence, as something you picked. That may feel like overclaiming. It isn't. The steering has been yours throughout, and the only thing missing is your own word on it — one sentence, where you can see it.
4.sheetLine: You've been heading somewhere by choice. Put your name on it.

1.tense: Right now, you are sharing what you have and steering where it goes.
1.verb: passing strength between people where the road asks for it
1.place: at the wheel, with a hand on the heading
1.ask: Take a call you keep polling and hold it for three days straight. Don't compare it, don't shop for a better option, don't reopen it. On the fourth morning you can look again.
1.core:
Right now you're carrying strength that moves between people, and you're sitting where the direction gets chosen. When a heading holds still, what you pass to others has a shape — those near it can lean on it because they can see where it points. That's the version that lasts.

What it costs to keep is leaving some roads closed. Take a call you keep polling — a plan, an offer, a way you keep surveying — and hold it for three days without reopening it. Nothing has to be announced. Nobody has to agree. The point isn't to force it; it's to let a single direction stand long enough to have a shape at all.
1.sheetLine: What you share gets a shape when the heading holds still.

2.tense: You are bracing toward a future you're trying to write in advance.
2.verb: passing strength between people where the road asks for it
2.place: at the wheel, with a hand on the heading
2.ask: Give back a small thing you've carried too long, before anyone brings it up. No note, no receipt, no mention that you did. Then drop the running count you keep about who's ahead.
2.core:
A future is being braced for, and the strength going out between people is being aimed by that brace. Support flips into supervision: what's handed over gets tallied, what's still owed gets watched, and generosity arrives with a hook in it. Those receiving it feel the hook even when they can't name it. That's the future arriving before it's earned.

Giving less is not the repair. The repair is to shut a book nobody agreed to. Hand back a small thing you've been holding too long and say nothing afterward. What comes back free after that is the kind of support that doesn't need a future to pay it off.
2.sheetLine: Give back the small thing you owe, and keep no count.

3.tense: You were once holding strength for people, and you're still at that door.
3.verb: passing strength between people where the road asks for it
3.place: at the wheel, with a hand on the heading
3.ask: Something finished still has your hand where the old heading was. Go once toward the part you've been dodging and stay long enough to find out what's actually there. An hour you choose, then decide.
3.core:
The strength that used to move between people has gone quiet. Not because you're weak — because the place it flowed from sits behind you now, and you're still facing it. New directions get picked up and put down without ever leaving the door. Those nearby feel the halt more than the reason.

The stand won't break on more effort. Take the part of the finished thing you've been dodging and go once toward it on purpose — the conversation, the room, the piece of work — long enough to feel whether it still holds anything or only holds the habit. An hour you choose. Then decide, with evidence, whether the commitment stays or drops.
3.sheetLine: It isn't gone. It's waiting at a door you already passed.

4.tense: The pen is down, and the hand that set the heading has already been writing.
4.verb: passing strength between people where the road asks for it
4.place: at the wheel, with a hand on the heading
4.ask: You've been steering by a plan you didn't sign off on again. Name a direction you actually want — not the sensible one — and take a step that only makes sense if that's where you're going. No announcement.
4.core:
A direction is being held without anyone admitting to holding it. Choices about where things go keep getting made, and the story around them is that they just sort of happened — the schedule, the offer, the move between people. The steering is real; it's just unsigned. People nearby are going by a heading you set and haven't claimed.

Claim one piece of it. Name a direction you actually want — the one you'd pick if nobody sensible were watching — and take a single step that only makes sense if that's where you're headed. Not a declaration, not a plan for anyone else. One move, and you'll be able to say to yourself that you chose it.
4.sheetLine: You've been steering a heading you haven't owned.

3.tense: You are at a door you already walked through, pen still in hand.
3.verb: sharing what your strength can carry
3.place: the place where you can tell what deserves your attention
3.ask: Take something you have been carrying purely out of loyalty and give it a real attempt this week, enough to learn whether it still holds you.
3.core:
The strength is still in you. It travels outward and does not come back, and no one seems to receive it as a gift anymore. Holding things up is what you do well, and there has been nothing on the far side of it. Whatever you have been keeping steady, you have kept steady alone, and the out-surge has gone one direction so long it no longer registers as generosity.

So test one of them. Choose something you carry out of loyalty or habit and put a real attempt behind it this week — enough that it either holds or it does not, and you will be able to tell which. If it holds, the strength returns into it. If it does not, you can set it down and meet what is actually here. The attempt is what answers. Nothing short of it will.
3.sheetLine: Test the old thing. Learn whether it holds.

4.tense: You are moving toward something particular and calling it keeping busy.
4.verb: sharing what your strength can carry
4.place: the place where you can tell what deserves your attention
4.ask: Next time the question comes, describe where this is going instead of how it has gone. No supporting record in the sentence.
4.core:
A direction runs under your strength that anyone near you can name. Asked what you are working toward, you describe what you have been managing — the shape of recent months, the thing that ran into the thing. The heading is real and already doing its work through you. Your answers leave the heading out, and the people close enough to ask can hear the gap, which is why they keep asking.

State the direction before your own accounting has earned it for you. Next time the question comes, describe where this is going instead of how it has gone, and stand behind that without support. The record does not need to ride in the sentence. Saying what you are actually steering toward is nothing more than the plain fact of it.
4.sheetLine: There is a heading under this. Call it that.

1.tense: What you carry is going out to the people who need it, and nothing is running dry.
1.verb: sharing your strength outward, by measure
1.place: tending something that is still growing
1.ask: Pick the one you'd keep if the rest had to go, and give it your next hour. Leave the others unanswered for now.
1.core:
You've got strength to hand out, and it's going where it's needed. People come to you mid-crisis and leave steadier, and you don't make a performance of it. Nothing is running dry, so nothing has to be rationed right now.

Caring for something still growing is half patience and half aim, and the aim is what's gone quiet. Looking over every option keeps you from putting weight behind one. Pick the one you'd keep if the rest had to go, and give it your next hour; leave the others unanswered for now. The ones you set down will still be there. What you aim at gets the force of your aiming.
1.sheetLine: Your strength is going out and nothing is running dry.

2.tense: Every tally you keep will leave someone short, and the pushing keeps going anyway.
2.verb: sharing your strength outward, by measure
2.place: tending something that is still growing
2.ask: Do one fair thing where nobody is watching, and make no record of what it settles.
2.core:
You're keeping the round of giving up, and keeping it takes everything you've got. Who needs what, who got less, what comes back — the tally runs without stopping. Fairness run this hard stops being fairness and becomes a load carried by one pair of shoulders, and the things you tend can feel the squeeze of it.

The weights you keep lifting are heavier than the ones you set down. Do one fair thing where nobody sees, and write it nowhere. That isn't lowering the standard; it's giving the standard an hour off from earning. You'll still know what's owed. You'll stop paying interest on it. What you did unseen can stand without your supervision.
2.sheetLine: The scorekeeping is crushing the thing it protects.

3.tense: What you used to tend sits behind a door you already walked past.
3.verb: sharing your strength outward, by measure
3.place: tending something that is still growing
3.ask: Go back to something you set down and stay with the part you've been avoiding. Not the whole job. Notice what's still yours after.
3.core:
The caring stopped reaching the things it was for. What you tend runs on old arrangements — you keep the schedule, you answer when asked, and the part that actually wants it to grow has gone quiet. That isn't coldness. It's a gate left shut so long it stopped looking like a gate.

Dedication gets tested by friction, not by comfort. Go back to something you set down and stay with the piece you've been avoiding — the hard part, not the whole job. You don't need to want it first. Wanting tends to arrive after contact, not before. Whatever holds after that is what you're committed to, and knowing it is worth more than the time.
3.sheetLine: Nothing has been reaching the things you used to tend.

4.tense: You are setting the direction of what you tend, and you are calling it drift.
4.verb: sharing your strength outward, by measure
4.place: tending something that is still growing
4.ask: Think about the thing you tend, hold a picture of what you'd want it to become by next year, and keep the picture without making it into a plan.
4.core:
The direction of what you tend is being set, and you don't count it as yours. A word here, a nudge there, what you let pass and what you quietly don't — those are choices, and they're adding up to a heading. Anyone asked would be told you go where the current goes. The thing itself has been following a course.

Wanting is the earlier form of steering, before any plan earns the name. Think about the thing you tend, hold a picture of what you'd want it to become a year out, and keep that picture without making it into a plan. Not a target, not a promise to anyone. Holding what you want beside you shows your hand was on the wheel, and it can start steering on purpose.
4.sheetLine: You've been steering and calling it drift.

1.tense: Right now, the strength you have is moving well — out to people, by measure, without being spent.
1.verb: sharing strength outward by measure — holding, giving, building what others stand on
1.place: the desk where patterns get made and structures are drawn
1.ask: Pick a direction you actually want — the one that looks right can wait. Hold it for three days and stop surveying. Notice what settles when you quit checking every option.
1.core:
When you're strong for other people, you don't just lend muscle. You put structure around it — how it moves, when, to whom. That's a kind of building, and it holds.

What grows this is choosing. One heading, held, instead of auditing every option and waiting for the clearest signal. You'll still be generous. You'll just be pointed somewhere, and the support becomes purposeful rather than available for whatever pulls at it. The quiet reliability others lean on starts to bear your fingerprints, not just your effort. Three days is enough to tell whether the direction was right. You don't need certainty first — you need a heading you actually want, and then the days confirm or correct it.
1.sheetLine: Pick one direction. Steer. Let the rest wait.

2.tense: Somewhere ahead of now, strength will need to move — and you're already projecting where, how, and who will need what.
2.verb: sharing strength outward by measure — holding, giving, building what others stand on
2.place: the desk where patterns get made and structures are drawn
2.ask: Settle a debt you've been carrying — a payment, a repair, an apology — quietly, without mentioning it. Close the count yourself and don't report it.
2.core:
You read needs fast. You're already three moves ahead, calculating what will be owed, what should flow where, who will need what next. That's not generosity running wild. It's fairness working overtime. The problem is timing: you're trying to settle accounts that haven't opened yet, and the strain shows in how much you brace.

What returns it: doing one fair thing quietly. Not a grand gesture, not something anyone will witness. The private certainty that you settled what you owed — to a person, a situation, yourself — with no one affirming it. That's what a compass does. It doesn't broadcast; it points. Practice that, and the forward-gaze relaxes. You don't have to manage where help goes next. You just settle what's actually yours and move on.
2.sheetLine: Settle one debt quietly. Let the ledger stay closed.

3.tense: Strength that used to flow outward is sitting still, and the pattern-making that once organized things feels done already.
3.verb: sharing strength outward by measure — holding, giving, building what others stand on
3.place: the desk where patterns get made and structures are drawn
3.ask: Take a commitment with a hard part you've been stepping around. Walk straight into that friction once — not to fix it, only to see what holds.
3.core:
You can still hold. Nothing's gone. But where you once shaped things — organized, provided, made it work — there's a stillness now, like what you built is waiting for someone else to need it.

The way back in isn't a push. It's a test. There's something you're committed to that has a friction point you've been avoiding, and the avoidance feels like wisdom but isn't. Walk into that friction once. Not to solve it — to feel whether your commitment survives contact. If it does, you'll know the strength is still yours and the direction is still true. If it doesn't, you've learned which commitment was habit and can let it go. Either way, something moves that was stuck. The release isn't defeat. It's what lets you hold the next thing without forcing it.
3.sheetLine: Walk into the hard part once. See what holds.

4.tense: The strength is moving outward, the structures are being made, and you'd tell anyone you're just keeping things running.
4.verb: sharing strength outward by measure — holding, giving, building what others stand on
4.place: the desk where patterns get made and structures are drawn
4.ask: Claim one heading you keep turning toward — a person, a project, a place — and hold it as a choice you made. Not a duty. Just true.
4.core:
Them: the people close to you are steadier because of something you do. You're organizing, providing, making it work. From your own telling, it's circumstance — the thing that needed doing, the role that was open, the one who couldn't hold it alone.

That's the miss. The shape you keep giving things is yours to claim, and the heading you steer by was picked, not assigned. You've been moving toward a light you haven't admitted you chose. Claiming one of them — one place you keep pouring into — as a decision, an orientation, not a duty, is the work. It doesn't change what you do. It changes who's doing it. The strength gets an owner, and the next time you turn toward that thing, you'll know it's because you chose to. That's the radiance: not effort, not sacrifice — just someone whose cultivation reached its shape and is shining on purpose.
4.sheetLine: Claim one direction as yours. You chose it.

1.tense: The strength is moving between people right now, and it is arriving where it is needed.
1.verb: passing strength along to whoever is holding something up
1.place: where meaning is carried forward between people — the habits, words and practices handed down and kept alive
1.ask: Choose what you will carry forward — a practice, a person, a piece of history — and this week put your hands on it, not your survey.
1.core:
You can hold a thing up and hand it on. What you have, you pass to whoever needs it, and the passing keeps it alive. Someone leaves with more than they came with because you stood there steady and shared what you had. That is the whole work: strength moving between people, spent on what matters rather than held.

What is free to feed next is direction. You can pick a heading — a practice, a person, a piece of history worth keeping — and give it your whole hands instead of half-attention here and there. The passing works better when it knows where it is going. Name the one thing this week and carry it deliberately; the rest can wait.
1.sheetLine: You pass strength along, and it keeps people standing.

2.tense: The sharing is running past itself, handing out strength before anyone has asked for it.
2.verb: passing strength along to whoever is holding something up
2.place: where meaning is carried forward between people — the habits, words and practices handed down and kept alive
2.ask: Think of a small debt you carry — a return, a favor, ground you took — and settle it before anyone asks.
2.core:
Sharing here can outrun the asking. Strength gets given before it is needed, pushed at people who did not reach, and what was support starts to feel like weight. The deciding happens before the moment arrives, for a future that has not come. What was holding turns into carrying that nobody requested.

Your inner sense of what is fair is the way back, and it does not need an audience. Somewhere in all this giving there is a small imbalance you have not settled — a thing owed, a share not returned, a claim you quietly hold. Find it and pay it where no one is watching. Fairness returns when the flow stops being one-directional and starts being exchange again, and exchange comes back one honest, private payment at a time.
2.sheetLine: You hand out strength faster than anyone can take it.

3.tense: The sharing stopped and the person stood at that door and stayed there.
3.verb: passing strength along to whoever is holding something up
3.place: where meaning is carried forward between people — the habits, words and practices handed down and kept alive
3.ask: Pick the part of this you have been avoiding — the difficult conversation, the unglamorous work, the commitment that keeps costing — and walk into it this week. See what holds.
3.core:
Where meaning is carried between people, not much is moving lately. The strength to share is real and present, and it is going nowhere. Standing back feels safer than reaching in, and the backing away has become the habit. Nothing new is being passed on. The hands that could hold something up are staying in pockets.

What returns this is not trying harder to care. It is walking straight into the part you have been avoiding and letting the friction tell you what you are actually committed to. Choose the hard conversation, the unglamorous task, the thing that costs. Do it once. What survives the doing is the commitment, and what falls away was only the method. This comes back after you have been tested, not before.
3.sheetLine: You stopped passing anything on, and stood back instead.

4.tense: You are carrying meaning forward between people, and your account of it is that you are simply present.
4.verb: passing strength along to whoever is holding something up
4.place: where meaning is carried forward between people — the habits, words and practices handed down and kept alive
4.ask: Name what you will carry forward — the reading, the habit, the person — and give your attention there only, letting the other surveys go.
4.core:
Something is being kept alive here because you keep it, and you would say you were just there when it happened. None of your part is being named as work. The meaning that gets passed between people gets passed through you. Your version has you as terrain rather than builder.

Before all this, you chose a direction and walked. Not because it made sense, because it pulled. Choose the heading again, plainly — the thing you will actually carry forward, chosen because you want it. Turning toward it, rather than weighing every option evenly, is where this began for you. The single direction makes the passing possible, and you get to name your part in it.
4.sheetLine: You are the one keeping it alive, and you would say you were only there.

1.tense: The support is moving now, clean and measured, with the pen in today's hand.
1.verb: sharing your strength
1.place: where connection forms between people
1.ask: Pick a heading for the support that matters most, chosen from wanting it rather than working it out, and move it a single step. No surveying the rest.
1.core:
The strength is going out and coming back. Something of yours is landing with the people near you, and it is not being spent just because it left your hands. You can watch it arrive and see it carried onward, which is why offering it does not scare you the way it once did. What you cultivate reaches a point of use, and the use is visible.

That is the balanced case, and the balance is not the whole of it. What wants feeding next is direction: the support is generous but it has no single heading. One step this week, along a line you chose on purpose, and then hold your hand. Do not turn it into a project. Name where a heading would come from in your own life, and take it. The rest of the support can keep flowing while you do.
1.sheetLine: The strength is shared and visible, and it wants one heading.

2.tense: You are reading the ledger before the moment arrives, seeing who will owe what before anyone has asked.
2.verb: sharing your strength
2.place: where connection forms between people
2.ask: For a week, keep track only of what you owe — nothing of what you are owed — and settle your part without asking anyone else to settle theirs.
2.core:
Support has turned into fairness, and the fairness has turned into a running account. You are already there with the calculator before the room has asked: who is short, who should step up, what you will do if they do not. The check is real, and it is costing the connection it was supposed to guard. People can feel the scale sitting between you and them.

Fixing this means going private with the fairness instead of public. Keep track only of what you owe and settle it, without balancing anyone else's account and without telling them what their share is. You will still know. Say a plain sentence when something is owed to you, once, and then let the matter close. What you owe is the only part that stays yours to discharge.
2.sheetLine: The accounting has outpaced the moment.

3.tense: Something ended, and the strength that used to go out now sits in a place it has left.
3.verb: sharing your strength
3.place: where connection forms between people
3.ask: Take up a hard piece of this that you have been avoiding, and find which part of your care is committed and which was only the form.
3.core:
You are standing at a threshold that closed behind you. The support used to leave your hands easily; now it stays. The people are there, and you are not reaching toward them, and the whole arrangement feels finished. You may not be able to say when it stopped. You do not have to.

A plant comes back through its roots, not through force. Take up a hard piece of this on purpose, small and on your own terms, and find which part of your care is committed and which was only the form. What holds, you keep. What does not hold, you drop the approach and not the commitment. The connection may return through the part of you that still wants it, in its own time, after you have stopped trying to force the threshold.
3.sheetLine: The care is still there and the reach has not come back.

4.tense: The alignment is already at work between you and them, and your own name for it is being easy.
4.verb: sharing your strength
4.place: where connection forms between people
4.ask: Face a single direction in this connection instead of surveying it — no comparing, no checking where the options stand — and see days later what moved without your management.
4.core:
The connection is in good order, and the order is not your doing. You would say the two of you just fit, that conversation is easy, that nothing is required. Something is moving a freely given strength between you, and it is not the result of you tending it. What is at work is a heading, and you have been treating it as coincidence. People near you can feel the difference.

Acknowledge the pull rather than the outcome. Face a single direction in this connection instead of surveying it — no comparing, no checking where the options stand — and see days later what moved without your management. You are not asked to announce anything. Knowing that a heading was yours is the whole act, and the strength stays one you can feel in your own hand.
4.sheetLine: The alignment is real, and you have been treating it as good luck.

1.tense: The strength you carry is already pointed at a goal and moving.
1.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
1.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling
1.ask: Give your first hour tomorrow to the aim you are actually headed for, before anything else gets a claim.
1.core:
You have more in you than most of the people near you can carry, and you have not made a fuss about it. It shows in how things get placed where they are needed, often before anyone asks. Where you are now, that is not only goodwill. There is a heading in it, and the heading came from you.

Put one aim on the line. Tomorrow, take the goal you are already walking toward and give it the first hour of the day. Nothing else gets that slot. No surveying, no re-deciding whether it is the right one. What this does is let the aim be seen from outside. Whoever is being carried starts to see what carries them, and the steering stops being something only you can hold.
1.sheetLine: You are aiming at something. Name it.

2.tense: This week you are bracing hard enough that the heading has no room left to be chosen.
2.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
2.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling
2.ask: Before anyone has to ask, return the thing you know belongs to another person — an object, an apology, money you borrowed.
2.core:
You can carry a lot, and you have started carrying it ahead of time. The load has moved into a future that has not arrived, and pushing is now the point. It shows. People get the help before they need it, or get asked a question they cannot answer yet. What was theirs to hold is being handled for them.

Go back to what is already owed. Not the large debt — the lesser one. Hand back the thing you know belongs to someone else before they have to ask. An object, an apology, money you borrowed, credit you took. Doing what is plainly fair sets your feet back down on today. Then the next hand you put out lands where it is actually wanted, not where you guessed it would be needed.
2.sheetLine: Return what you are holding for someone else.

3.tense: The heading you were following stopped back there, and you have been standing beside it since.
3.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
3.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling
3.ask: If one way you push at something has gone dead, drop that method and stay with the purpose it was for.
3.core:
The drive has backed up. You can feel it. What was moving is not moving, and you have gone quiet about that. Strength is still there, but it is not being aimed anywhere, so it drains off through small jobs and short answers. What looked like holding still has become a door you have already walked past.

Test the commitment without the friction of the old method. Take something you have been pushing at in a set way, and put the method down. Keep the purpose. A different route to the same goal, a different hour, a different person to ask, a smaller version of the same move. The test is whether anything at all is still pulling you forward, or only the way you used to do it. The pull returns once you stop wrestling the door.
3.sheetLine: The direction stopped. The aim has not.

4.tense: You are already pointing at something, and you have been telling people you are still looking.
4.verb: hand the next thing forward before it is asked for
4.place: where momentum is pointed at a goal and everything is already rolling
4.ask: Let your next real choice follow what you want rather than what makes the best sense, and watch what it brings.
4.core:
There is a heading in you that keeps appearing in what you reach for, who you take seriously, where your money and hours go. Your name for it has been keeping options open. Anyone watching can see where you are pointed. So can you, when nobody is asking.

Let it be decided once without arguing the case first. Take the next real decision and act on what you want, not on what holds up best on paper. Small is fine. Where the free afternoon goes, who you say yes to, which draft you start, which door you let close. If it turns out wrong, you will still know the heading was real, and that is worth more to the next decision than another month of surveying.
4.sheetLine: You are already pointed. Say the heading.

1.tense: Right now you are carrying what needs carrying and it is moving between people the way it should.
1.verb: Carrying more than your own weight so the people near you stay upright.
1.place: Where you keep bearing what has to be borne and keep your form under it.
1.ask: Decide on a direction you want more of a year from now, and give it thirty minutes this week — no surveying the rest.
1.core:
You can carry what has to be carried and pass strength to the people near you in the same motion. It isn't hardness. You keep your shape under pressure without going stiff, so somebody's rough week can land on you and you stay level and hand something back that helps. Carrying and giving are one movement here, which is what makes it work.

What you feed with that strength is worth deciding rather than inheriting. The weight you take on for others is already settled; where the whole of you points next is not. Go by what you actually want, not what logic says it is sensible to want, and hold that heading through the first three days, when the pull is strongest and the newness is gone. It holds because you chose it.
1.sheetLine: You carry the weight and pass the strength on.

2.tense: You are bracing under a load that has not actually landed on you yet.
2.verb: Carrying more than your own weight so the people near you stay upright.
2.place: Where you keep bearing what has to be borne and keep your form under it.
2.ask: The next time the urge to pre-solve someone's problem shows up, do the small fair move your compass gives you, then leave the rest with them.
2.core:
The strength going out from you gets to people before the moment they need it. You sense a problem forming a week off and start bearing it now, so the people beside you get steadiness before they have asked and sometimes before they know anything is wrong. The support is real. It has stopped waiting to be received, and you keep checking whether you are giving the right amount, which is the calculation all of this was meant to spare you.

When over-giving shows up in a small case, follow the compass once and stop. The person on the other end gets room to do their own part for once. Fairness that moves freely does not keep a running tally; it makes one honest move and then lets go. What contains without crushing is what you are reaching back toward.
2.sheetLine: You're bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived.

3.tense: Somewhere behind this moment you were holding your shape under pressure and today nothing is asking that of you.
3.verb: Carrying more than your own weight so the people near you stay upright.
3.place: Where you keep bearing what has to be borne and keep your form under it.
3.ask: Spend twenty minutes today on the hard part of something you keep circling — the actual difficulty, not the setting up.
3.core:
Endurance is in you. You have carried weight before. Right now nothing is calling on it, and you stay a step back from the difficult part, watching it, keeping the forms up. The people who lean on you get a version of your strength. Not the full one. The firm ability to hold under load is still there, waiting, and it is not being asked for.

Go at the difficult thing on purpose, not by getting tougher first. Twenty minutes of real friction will tell you more than another week of getting ready. Some of it will hold. Some will turn out to have been the wrong shape and fall away, which is how the thing worth committing to gets found. The commitment is what gets tested. The method is what gets dropped.
3.sheetLine: You've carried it before. Today you stand beside it.

4.tense: The strength is moving between people and you are telling it as though someone else brought it.
4.verb: Carrying more than your own weight so the people near you stay upright.
4.place: Where you keep bearing what has to be borne and keep your form under it.
4.ask: Aim at something you have been quietly moving toward. Say nothing about it. Give it three days before you decide.
4.core:
You are the one holding the line several people are currently standing behind. Ask and you would say it just kept things steady, that anyone would have done it. The people being held have not made that mistake — they know where the weight came from. What is missing is not the doing. It is your own account of it, and the direction running underneath, which has been steering without your attention on it.

There is a heading in you that took shape before you had words for it and has been setting the course with nobody watching. Put your attention there. Something you have been moving toward while telling yourself you were only handling what came up. Three days facing one way will show you what was already true. The turn comes before anyone else's.
4.sheetLine: You're holding it up and calling it someone else's.

1.tense: You are here, with the pen, and your strength moves out between people cleanly.
1.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
1.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill
1.ask: At your practice today, settle what you're building toward, and aim the whole session there instead of ranging across everything.
1.core:
You have a steady way of turning your strength outward, sharing what you carry with whoever can use it, and right now it is working. The practice has settled, and what you have cultivated shows up in what you can hand over. The small light you keep lit by attention is enough to be seen by.

Give the practice a heading. Decide what you are building toward — a skill, a number, a particular line of work — and let each session bend toward that rather than survey all of it. Wanting something specific is allowed, and it is what gives the sharing a shape a coworker or a friend can aim at. Direction doesn't narrow what you hand over; it makes handing it over intentional.
1.sheetLine: You give well when you know what you're building toward.

2.tense: You are braced for a day that is not here yet, and the strength spills into it early.
2.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
2.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill
2.ask: When somebody's owed a small thing and your gut says settle it, do that today without writing it in the tally.
2.core:
You are working from the idea that if you don't hold everything up, it comes down. The practice has turned into a night watch, and the sharing has turned into supplying. What you are bracing against has not happened. From your seat the work looks like staying on top of a bad day whose outline you can already feel, and the strength you push at the room lands harder than you intended.

Let your own sense of what's fair settle the small case. When a little thing is owed — a reply, a fiver, something borrowed — do what seems right and skip the log. Fairness that moves doesn't keep count. Your grip can ease one notch and the room stays standing, because your strength was the steady part, not the force in it.
2.sheetLine: Loosen the grip and the room still stands.

3.tense: You are still standing in front of a door you already walked through.
3.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
3.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill
3.ask: Take a single piece of your practice that has stopped working, set just that piece down, and keep the practice going.
3.core:
The practice went quiet somewhere in the last stretch. What you were building toward faded, and the sharing that used to flow got shut down in a way you did not quite author yourself. From where you sit the strength looks gone. Underneath, the commitment is still there, waiting on a way of doing it that no longer fits who you are now.

Let the friction show you what to drop, not what to abandon. Take a method that isn't working — an hour, a tool, the shape of the routine — and set it down. Keep the commitment itself. When something has genuinely finished, releasing it isn't defeat. The practice is clearing space for the next thing it will carry.
3.sheetLine: What you're committed to can outlive how you were doing it.

4.tense: The practice is already being steered, and the heading has not been written anywhere yet.
4.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
4.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill
4.ask: Pick the point of your session by what you actually want, not by the sensible argument, and put that line in the notebook.
4.core:
You have been shaping the practice by what seems reasonable — the schedule, the argument, the sensible step — while something in you has been moving toward a different mark. Were you asked, you would say you were following the logic. The practice is following a want. The direction is being written by your own hand, and nobody has signed it, you included.

Name it. Before the session starts, settle what the whole thing is for out of what you actually want — the skill, the person, the version of yourself you have in mind — and put that line in the notebook. The line does the acknowledging. Once the heading is on paper, the strength you share has a reason the person receiving it can see.
4.sheetLine: You're steering it already. One line makes it yours.

1.tense: What you have is moving out toward people in measured amounts, and you get to aim it.
1.verb: course strength outward to whoever needs it
1.place: at the door where what was outside is arriving
1.ask: Fix on one real place this help should go — one person, one use — and steer only there.
1.core:
Something wants to be met at the door, and strength already leaves you toward where it's needed. It reaches people in amounts they can actually use. None of this is for show; the supply is real and it's measured, which is exactly what keeps it going instead of leaving you empty in a week.

What keeps it clean is having a bearing. Help with a direction lands as help; help without one scatters and reads as noise, and nobody can tell what to do with it. Before the next request reaches you, take a minute to know what this strength is for this season, so the help you hand over has a shape and doesn't just answer whoever calls the loudest. The bearing can change later. A season is enough.
1.sheetLine: Help aimed somewhere holds its shape.

2.tense: You are rehearsing tomorrow's needs before anything has arrived at the door today.
2.verb: course strength outward to whoever needs it
2.place: at the door where what was outside is arriving
2.ask: Before you answer what arrives once today, stand still a minute and let your own sense of what's fair decide, not the stack of what might be owed.
2.core:
What is entering hasn't asked for anything yet, and the door is already held wide, the future run through, provisions set for a need that hasn't knocked. The strength that should travel by measure is running out past the moment. The pace you're keeping belongs to a later hour, and it costs you the hour you're actually in.

Under the tallying there's a plain knowing of what's fair in a given case, before the counting starts. Standing still for a minute before you act on what arrives is enough to hear it. That minute isn't hesitation. It's what separates meeting the moment from overriding it. Try it once, and see whether the moment still needs the same answer you were about to give.
2.sheetLine: You're holding a door nothing has knocked on yet.

3.tense: You were offering a form of help that the moment needing it had already left behind.
3.verb: course strength outward to whoever needs it
3.place: at the door where what was outside is arriving
3.ask: Find one way you still offer support that isn't landing. Put that shape down — keep the care underneath and show up differently.
3.core:
The source at this door has been low for some time, and strength keeps leaving it anyway. What you hand over isn't there to give, and nothing returns, and after enough of that the offering grates in your hands. There's a version of help you've kept up past the point where it fit: same gesture, same shape, no longer landing. The commitment under it was real. The form is finished.

Let the grating tell you something. When a way of helping moves through you and rasps, that friction is information, not failure. Keep the care, put down the shape, and let what replaces it be smaller and truer than the last one. Something was supposed to come through this door, and you were standing in it handing out what had already drained away.
3.sheetLine: You keep handing over what left you a while back.

4.tense: Your strength is already pointing somewhere, and you have not named the direction as your own.
4.verb: course strength outward to whoever needs it
4.place: at the door where what was outside is arriving
4.ask: Pick the direction this strength already leans and face it for a week, quitting the survey of other options. Look again at the end.
4.core:
Something is arriving, and your hands are already set for it: you steady people, you make room, your presence gets quieter when someone needs space. None of that registers as a decision. It arrives as the way things are. There's a direction in it that you set and have not claimed as yours, and leaving it unclaimed keeps it from being anything you can steer by.

What you do is real; the story you tell about it is thin. When the next choice comes about where this strength goes, turn toward the direction you actually want and stand there for a week. Quit surveying the others. Facing the way your help already leans turns it into a bearing instead of a reflex, and the bearing is the part that was missing.
4.sheetLine: The direction is yours. It just hasn't been called that.

1.tense: Right now the weight between you is where it should be, and you carry your share without keeping score.
1.verb: spending your own strength so the ones beside you can stand
1.place: where the load between two people gets weighed and corrected
1.ask: Point your effort one direction this week — your own pick, not the place it's needed most — and work there, letting the other things wait.
1.core:
Strength moves between you and the ones you're beside, and the amounts come out right. What you put in returns, nobody carries more than their part, and that's what keeps it steady. Steady like this, it's free to feed direction: not strength spread thinner over more of them, but strength aimed at something on purpose.

So pick the heading before the week fills up. One direction for your own effort, chosen because you want it, not because somebody's short. Then stop scanning the room for what else needs you. You'll feel the pull to keep looking — things you've been holding will wave from the side. Let them wave. What you already carry stays yours; the new part is only the aim. Keep the load fair while you're at it, because fair is what makes aiming last.
1.sheetLine: The weight is fair, and now your strength can be aimed.

2.tense: In the weeks ahead you'll be watching the scales before anything has been asked of you, keeping shares even on paper nobody asked to see.
2.verb: spending your own strength so the ones beside you can stand
2.place: where the load between two people gets weighed and corrected
2.ask: At the next small debt — a few dollars, a favor, a reply owed — settle it once from gut sense and stop, closing the ledger there.
2.core:
You give so the weights come out even, and you're already checking the next several rounds in advance. Every gap gets measured before it opens. From outside it looks generous; from inside it doesn't land, because a scale that keeps wanting to be checked can't rest, and neither can the ones standing on it.

There's a steadier place to run this from: the quiet sense of what's right that doesn't need arithmetic. Settle one small debt this week — money, a returned favor, a reply you owe — from that sense, once, and leave the record of it alone. You'll feel the pull to audit it by Thursday. Let the audit go. The evenness you've been buying with all that measuring is already in your hands.
2.sheetLine: You're weighing shares that haven't been asked for yet.

3.tense: The flow of strength between you and the ones beside you stopped moving awhile back, and you're still at the old arrangement.
3.verb: spending your own strength so the ones beside you can stand
3.place: where the load between two people gets weighed and corrected
3.ask: Set something you still hold for someone against real resistance this week — the awkward ask, the true number — and let what happens tell you what holds.
3.core:
What passes between you and the others has gone quiet. The arrangement you had still stands in your head, but nothing moves through it now. You keep your own, and wait to find out whether re-entering is worth it. It isn't a choice you made — it's a doorway you've been standing at since it shut.

The way through isn't more giving, and it isn't feeling your way in. Take one commitment you still carry and set it against something that pushes back — the part you've been steering around because it might end. Maybe it ends. Maybe it holds. Either way the testing is the point, and whatever falls away was the method, not the commitment. Let something meet real resistance this week and see what holds.
3.sheetLine: What passed between you went quiet, and you're waiting at the door.

4.tense: The balancing keeps happening through your hands, and your own account of it names luck instead of you.
4.verb: spending your own strength so the ones beside you can stand
4.place: where the load between two people gets weighed and corrected
4.ask: When you catch yourself setting something right between two people, hold a second and know your hand is in it, then do it anyway — no announcement.
4.core:
You re-balance things for the ones near you — absorb the shortfall, step back, say the sentence that settles it — and it doesn't register as anything done. It's just how the room goes. The hand on the scale is yours; your words for it are mood, timing, chemistry. The ones on the other end don't file it that way.

Nothing needs announcing, and nothing needs discussing. Steer the direction you already steer and stop checking whether it counts. When you're setting something even without a word, hold a beat and register that the correction is coming from you, then make it anyway. One second of knowing, and the skill stops being background. The weighing was yours the whole time. Only the name was missing.
4.sheetLine: The hand evening things out is yours, filed under luck.

1.tense: Right now, strength you have built up is finding its way to someone who needs it.
1.verb: sharing your strength where it is needed
1.place: setting down what has run its course
1.ask: Decide which person or project this strength is for, and give toward it for a week without second-guessing the choice.
1.core:
What you can do here is know what you've been developing and share the strength from it clearly, by measure. Nothing about that needs arranging or announcing — it moves because the work behind it is real, and the people receiving it can tell that apart from a gesture.

Next time you're deciding who gets what, hold the question for a minute first. Which light are you actually steering by? A direction you've chosen doesn't need defending once it's chosen; it needs you to keep handing toward it while the week runs. That's slower than answering whoever asks first, and the ones who receive from you will feel the difference over time.
1.sheetLine: Strength that's ready flows toward the one who needs it.

2.tense: Soon enough you'll be reading the scales on support that has not had a chance to land yet.
2.verb: sharing your strength where it is needed
2.place: setting down what has run its course
2.ask: Let your own sense of what's fair settle one small question of who gets what — nobody watching — and act before you check it with anyone.
2.core:
When strength moves between people here, some part of you is already counting what's owed: who has had more, who has had less, what a fair share looks like before anyone has asked. Sharing gets heavier than it needs to be. What should flow has to pass a scale first.

Your own sense of what is right is still in there, and it can close a small case quietly. Give it one practice case you don't have to weigh: return what you owe, say the fair thing, and leave the tally alone. The count can wait until morning. What you hand over after checking fares worse for the checking, and people feel the calculation in it.
2.sheetLine: You weigh what you give before it can leave your hands.

3.tense: Strength meant to move between people is sitting still, and you are the one holding it.
3.verb: sharing your strength where it is needed
3.place: setting down what has run its course
3.ask: Take the hard part you have been circling and sit with it once. Only that piece. Notice what holds while you're in it.
3.core:
Where strength moves between people, it has gone quiet. You can see what's needed and you're not the one handing it over. This isn't stinginess — the impulse to give is still in you, aimed at nothing at the moment, and the room around it has gone flat.

What survives this isn't a decision; it's an old practice. Going back to the hard part for one sitting isn't a rescue and isn't a defeat. It shows you what's worth your strength, and what holds when you're inside it. Pick the practice back up for its own sake, not because someone needs saving. Support doesn't come back by deciding to care more; it comes back by doing one true thing.
3.sheetLine: You can see what's needed and set your strength down.

4.tense: Here, strength is leaving you steadily, and the hand steering it has not been claimed.
4.verb: sharing your strength where it is needed
4.place: setting down what has run its course
4.ask: Choose one direction for your strength this week because you want it, not because the week needs it — then hold that choice without explaining it to anyone.
4.core:
You keep people and projects upright, and from inside your story it just happens that way. The strength you share has a direction, but the one who chose it isn't claiming the choice. Whatever you were aiming for sits somewhere else in the account.

Try settling on the direction once: the place you're steering toward because you chose it, not because it's sensible. Then hold it without justifying it to anyone. Nobody else has to know, and you can drop it tomorrow if it doesn't fit. Sharing runs on knowing where you're pointed, and that knowing is yours — to keep or to put down. That's the part that's gone unspoken, and it's the only part.
4.sheetLine: Strength leaves you steadily. The one steering it is unclaimed.

1.tense: You are here with the pen, and the sharing moves at the size it should.
1.verb: sharing strength outward, by measure
1.place: at the edge of an ending that clears the room
1.ask: Choose the heading you want this week and hold it for three days — no spread, no yes to every request that arrives.
1.core:
When someone close to you is short of something, your hands already know the right amount to pass over. Not a rescue, not a token — just what this person can carry and what you can spare. You don't make a project of it. What you pass along holds because it was sized to the person, not to the volume of the need, and the ones on the receiving end can feel the difference.

Before the next request sets your direction, choose the heading from what you want, not from the logic of who sounds most desperate. Hold that line for three days. Saying yes to each request that comes means no direction at all. One clear line beats an even spread — that is what this clearing is asking of you.
1.sheetLine: You share by measure, and people can tell the difference.

2.tense: You are bracing against an ending that hasn't happened, and you are the one holding the door.
2.verb: sharing strength outward, by measure
2.place: at the edge of an ending that clears the room
2.ask: Pay one small debt you know is real, quietly, and notice which account stops asking once it is settled.
2.core:
Here the sharing has gone past measure. Something is being kept alive that already finished — a role, a standing obligation, a way of holding it together — and the cost is being paid by your body, quietly. You give where you think you still owe, when nothing is owed, and the shape of it gets harder to keep in view. The tally runs on in you and it is not producing fairness, only heat, and the ones near you can feel that heat without knowing its source.

Settle the small account that is actually yours. Pay the one debt that is real, and leave the ones that only exist in your arithmetic alone — that is the fair call here, not the tidy one. Watch what happens to the tally once one line is closed.
2.sheetLine: You're holding open a door that finished closing.

3.tense: You are standing at a door that closed a while back, and you haven't noticed.
3.verb: sharing strength outward, by measure
3.place: at the edge of an ending that clears the room
3.ask: Drop one way you have been showing up for people that has stopped landing, and keep the caring itself.
3.core:
Something came to an end here, and what you are doing now is insisting on the old form of it. The strength is still in you. Nothing moves from you to anyone, because the way you used to hand it over no longer fits where you are. There is no lack of resources — there is a grip on one method that has finished its work.

What gets released is not the caring, it is the one approach. Drop what isn't landing any more, and try one different version this week, once, with one person. If the new shape lands, you'll know what the old one was hiding. Keep the purpose; let the method go.
3.sheetLine: It stopped moving because you're holding the old shape.

4.tense: You are already writing in this room, and your account has the pen elsewhere.
4.verb: sharing strength outward, by measure
4.place: at the edge of an ending that clears the room
4.ask: Before the next request sets your direction, decide where you actually want to head — and make a choice from there.
4.core:
The endings have been happening — a role finished, a phase closed, an arrangement fallen away — and your telling calls it circumstances. Somebody cleared that room, and it was you. The direction the clearing points is yours, made out of your own want, and your version leaves you out of it. You describe yourself as the one who happened to be there when it happened.

Steer by something you actually want, before the next request sets your heading for you. Decide where you want to head — on paper, or to yourself — and make a choice this week from that want rather than from who needs what. Your direction is what kept the ground under theirs. Own that, and the room stays yours.
4.sheetLine: The endings were your work, and your account leaves you out.

1.tense: The strength now moves out and comes back in the same steady breath.
1.verb: sharing strength by measure
1.place: a live tuning point
1.ask: Pick one aim for the next ten minutes and move toward it without surveying the room. Go the whole stretch before you decide whether it was right.
1.core:
You have an arrangement where carrying someone else does not hollow you out. What goes out comes back, the give and take stays roughly level, and the care keeps its quality because you are not deciding it from dread.

What holds this up is that you stay awake to the moment — how much, when, whether the other person is open right now. That is not coldness; that is attention. What comes next is a heading. Not only being the one who can hold things up, but knowing which way you are facing while you do it. The low pull under all this is a genuine wanting, and it sharpens when what you carry is clean.

When helping starts costing you your bones, the measure has tilted. That is a signal to adjust, not a verdict.
1.sheetLine: You hold things up without losing yourself. Keep the measure true.

2.tense: A future is being run that cannot be written in yet.
2.verb: sharing strength by measure
2.place: a live tuning point
2.ask: Do one unglamorous fair thing tonight with nobody aware of it. Do it once, then put it out of your mind entirely.
2.core:
You are bracing so hard for a future you cannot see that you are bolting the present shut. Support is steady when it moves from a quiet, natural sense of what is right. Right now it is not moving; it is being forced. You are checking crates against a scale that does not exist yet, and your hands are clenched around whatever might slip.

That is not open-handedness, it is defense. The care you are trying to secure is getting squeezed out of reach. What you actually want underneath is exchange that flows, not tallying that keeps starting up again. So find something plainly right, do it, and then let the counting stop. When you catch yourself auditing, ask whose scale this is. The strength loosens when it is not being tested at the gate.
2.sheetLine: You can't brace a future that hasn't happened. Let the now be true.

3.tense: You are still at a door you already walked through.
3.verb: sharing strength by measure
3.place: a live tuning point
3.ask: Sit with the task you keep sliding past for ten minutes, clumsily. Let it show you what is actually there without asking it for anything.
3.core:
The support went hollow. What used to be a shared resource now feels like a closed box you cannot open, and you are standing where it used to be, wondering why it is cold. Strength ran out of places to go and just pooled.

This is not a failure of your generosity. It is that you gave everything you had and did not keep a tap for yourself. The fix is not to force more out — that would empty you further. Instead, turn to the piece you have been sidestepping and handle it directly. Not for anyone else. For the practice of it. See what holds when nothing is watching. Ease might come in small steps, and you will know it by the release, not the applause.
3.sheetLine: You still help. But you left the room. Come back to the work.

4.tense: You are holding the pen down in a room where you are still writing.
4.verb: sharing strength by measure
4.place: a live tuning point
4.ask: For the next small choice today, follow what you want instead of what reasons best. Notice that you made the call yourself once it is done.
4.core:
Something in you is already steering the flow of help, but you are calling it 'what needs to happen' and stepping out of the frame. The strength that shares by measure is being pointed by someone, and that someone is you.

The generosity is real. What is off is subtle: you keep telling it that it is just circumstance. The truth is that you are deciding which needs are yours to carry. That is choosing, not accident. To take it back, do not thrash around trying to control more. Instead, sit still and ask what you actually want to move toward. The call is already being made at a level you are not watching. Bring it into the light, and the same action becomes chosen instead of automatic. Then the strength can glow from genuine development, not hidden drift.
4.sheetLine: You're making the call. Start saying so.

1.tense: Your hands are open right now, and what you have moves toward where it runs short.
1.verb: strength shared by measure
1.place: where the pattern shows, apart from any one case
1.ask: Pick one person you already help, and name to yourself what you want their year to move toward. Then let this week's help follow that.
1.core:
Someone near you is short of what you have, and you take in the whole shape of it — the gap, the handoff, what closes it. You do that without a speech, and they come out steadier for it. That is strength on its way out of you, by measure, not spilling. It goes well where you can be generous without keeping a tally, where it doesn't dim you, and where the one receiving it ends up more able rather than smaller.

Pick one person you already help and say to yourself what you want their life to point toward — not just this week's repair. Then let what you hand over follow that. Help gets lighter when it has a direction to travel in, and you'll spot sooner the point where it stopped being a gift and became a job.
1.sheetLine: Your strength goes where it's short, and no one has to ask twice.

2.tense: The whole map of who will run short is running ahead of you, and you will have supplies matched before anyone speaks.
2.verb: strength shared by measure
2.place: where the pattern shows, apart from any one case
2.ask: When you notice yourself totting up what someone is owed, make the small fair call and keep it to yourself. No explanation after.
2.core:
You can see a need coming before it lands — who will run short, what it costs, where the hole opens. That sight is real. It has also started deciding for you, so you show up with the answer built and no room left for whoever is actually there. The generosity is intact; it just moves faster than the situation does, and now and then it spends something you needed on a case you forecast.

When the totting-up starts, make the small fair call you already feel and say nothing about it. That private compass doesn't need a case argued. Holding the strength back instead of pressing it out is the practice here — one quiet fair call, kept quiet, no follow-up speech.
2.sheetLine: You see who'll come up short and you've started deciding for them.

3.tense: You gave what you had where it was needed, and the handing over ran on past the point where you were met.
3.verb: strength shared by measure
3.place: where the pattern shows, apart from any one case
3.ask: Take the piece of this you've been going around, and stay with it once, on purpose. Keep what you're committed to; the way you've been doing it can go.
3.core:
The pattern still reads clear to you — you see what's needed about as well as you ever did — but nothing underneath it is pushing the strength out anymore. The help leaves you flatter now, in a way you don't bring up, and toward some people you give to, you've quit expecting much back. What used to feed all this was finishing something, and lately a lot has been started toward others with nothing closed.

Go at the hard piece you've been routing around, once, deliberately. Not more effort and not more feeling — commitment tested against friction is what puts strength back in your hands. Keep the commitment; let go of the approach, of the method you reached for. Those may be two different things.
3.sheetLine: The pattern still reads clear. Nothing behind it is pushing the strength out.

4.tense: You are holding the whole pattern level, and you would tell anyone it simply holds that way.
4.verb: strength shared by measure
4.place: where the pattern shows, apart from any one case
4.ask: Take the thing you want, not what the situation wants, and keep that heading for three days. Don't take its measure in between.
4.core:
You keep people supplied, and you read the board well enough that it looks like nothing. Habit, you'd say, if asked. The level floor in your circle has your hands in it, and reading the situation well is part of how you place what you have. That is strength leaving you, outward. It only goes unseen by you; the ones who take it up have noticed right along.

Take the thing you want, rather than what the moment seems to need, and hold that heading for three days. Don't check how it's measuring up along the way. Having something of your own to move toward is what keeps the offering steady — and if you keep it in view, the ones around you tend to steady up too.
4.sheetLine: You say it just holds. The ones taking it up know better.

1.tense: The strength you pass around is flowing to the people who need it right now.
1.verb: sharing your strength with whoever needs it
1.place: where something that couldn't hold is coming down
1.ask: Settle the one aim your help is for this season, and steer your strength toward it instead of spreading thin.
1.core:
You hand people what they need without making a show of it, and the strength lands where it's needed. The condition for that is finishing something of your own first; the light comes off work that reached an end, not off effort. It's the plainest kind of giving there is: what got made, handed over.
A structure near you is coming down, and that's a clearing, not a loss. Give the flow one direction this time. Settle on what your help is for — an aim you'd still pick next year — and steer toward it. A river that runs one way moves more than one that spreads across a whole field. Your strength will reach further this season than it has in a year, because it goes somewhere on purpose.
1.sheetLine: Your strength flows outward. Give it one direction.

2.tense: Your strength will be spread over so many people that none of it will arrive whole.
2.verb: sharing your strength with whoever needs it
2.place: where something that couldn't hold is coming down
2.ask: Pick one person you're carrying and work out what you actually owe them, then settle it before anyone asks.
2.core:
The watchman doesn't sit down. When the structure comes down, every hand it was holding looks like your job, and you move in before anyone asks. You give before you've checked what's actually owed, so the help outruns the arithmetic.
Fairness isn't the fast part; it's the inside one. Keep your own count of what's owed in one place this week — who you're carrying, and whether it's yours to carry — and settle one of them before anyone mentions it. The count catches what haste skips. And don't add to what's already coming down just to keep holding it up. That's the way back.
2.sheetLine: You give before you've counted. Count first.

3.tense: You stopped offering your strength when the last thing you held came apart.
3.verb: sharing your strength with whoever needs it
3.place: where something that couldn't hold is coming down
3.ask: Name the commitment you're still true to and try a different way of keeping it this week, seeing what holds.
3.core:
The clearing did you in. You were carrying people when it happened, and after that you stopped bracing — no more hands out, no more arriving early. The strength is still in you, standing back where nothing can be asked of it, and the work that made it is unfinished.
What's gone is the method, not the purpose — the old way of holding no longer stands, and you're treating that as the end. Pick a commitment you're still true to, and try keeping it a different way this week. The friction tells you what's still yours, and the strength comes back through the doing, not around it. You don't decide your way out of this one; you find out by moving.
3.sheetLine: The strength is still there, waiting to be asked for.

4.tense: You have quietly been steering people well without calling it direction.
4.verb: sharing your strength with whoever needs it
4.place: where something that couldn't hold is coming down
4.ask: Take the heading you'd pick for your own work if nobody were weighing in, and face it three days without reopening the question.
4.core:
People come out of your company with a clearer idea of what to do, and you'd say you only listened. The truth is you know which way each of them should turn, and you carry that quietly. You haven't said the word for what you want, and it keeps working anyway, unclaimed.
The heading is already there; you steer by it without leaving the survey. Take the direction you'd pick for your own work if nobody were weighing in, and face it three days without reopening the question. Then move. The light doesn't come from more reading of the sky; it comes from facing one way long enough to find out. Finish your own work, not just your help.
4.sheetLine: You already steer by something. Name it and hold it.

1.tense: Right now you hand your strength out where it is needed, by measure, without emptying yourself.
1.verb: shares strength outward by measure
1.place: the pull toward the light you steer by
1.ask: Decide what most deserves your effort and put your hands only there this week, letting every other worthy cause go unfunded without an apology.
1.core:
You help well by measure, and what you help has an edge to it. It shows when something you built reaches a point you can name, and the help leaves your hands because it is finished, not because someone finally asked hard enough. People can tell what they get from you is weighed, and it lands with heft, not like a bill.

What this balance is free to feed next is aim. Decide what most deserves your effort and put your hands only there this week, letting every other worthy cause go unfunded without an apology. You are fluent enough that this will cost you, and the cost is the point. Reach is not direction, and the heading is yours to name.
1.sheetLine: You help by measure, and what you help has an edge.

2.tense: Soon you will be pouring strength out faster than anyone asked, bracing against a shortfall that has not arrived yet.
2.verb: shares strength outward by measure
2.place: the pull toward the light you steer by
2.ask: Let something owed be paid back quietly this week — a repair, a wrong put right, a debt settled — and keep it unmentioned afterward.
2.core:
Your help moves before the need does. An outcome you can foresee, someone's shortfall you can forecast, and your hands are already in motion — help arriving before the ask, before the person has felt the gap. From the inside it is care with good aim. From where they stand it reads as a bill nobody has been handed yet.

Let something owed be paid back quietly this week — a repair, a wrong put right, a debt settled — and keep it unmentioned afterward. What you owe and what you are owed can even out with nobody watching the scale. A single entry made unseen shows you what the flow feels like when the spout is not on display.
2.sheetLine: You're paying a bill nobody has handed you yet.

3.tense: Part of you stopped short at a door you had already walked through, and the help has run thin since.
3.verb: shares strength outward by measure
3.place: the pull toward the light you steer by
3.ask: Go at the part of something you care about that you keep avoiding, on purpose, and notice which pieces hold when friction arrives.
3.core:
There is a threshold behind you, and some of you has not crossed it. Strength still moves outward, but the measure has gone slack — help given a little late, a little thin, without the old aim under it. It is not that you stopped caring. It is that you have been waiting for a permission that stopped being required.

Go at the part of something you care about that you keep avoiding, on purpose, and notice which pieces hold when friction arrives. Not the whole wall. A single hard stone. Whichever parts hold under real load are the ones worth your name on them, and the rest you will find you stopped needing. Friction tells you which commitments are load-bearing.
3.sheetLine: A door shut behind you and part of you waits at it.

4.tense: The heading you steer by was chosen long before now, and you go on giving it shape without calling it chosen.
4.verb: shares strength outward by measure
4.place: the pull toward the light you steer by
4.ask: Face a single direction for three days and stop checking the others — no glancing back to see if the light still looks good.
4.core:
You steer by a heading picked well before this. The aim in your help, the measure in what you share, what makes it through and what does not — much of it was set early, and if asked you would say you just go where the light happens to be. The question doesn't come up, you'd say. It comes up whenever anyone raises it. The pull is registered. The hand on the wheel is unclaimed.

Face a single direction for three days and stop checking the others — no glancing back to see if the light still looks good. Say, if someone asks, that you chose it, then live that small. Not because the old choice was wrong, but because a heading nobody claims is one you could drift from without noticing.
4.sheetLine: You're still steering by a heading chosen long ago.

1.tense: You are giving from a full place, and it is landing where it is needed.
1.verb: share your strength where it is actually needed
1.place: in the fog where the next step is visible but the road is not
1.ask: Pick the heading your help takes this week — where it matters most — and follow that one. Other places can stay open until the next week.
1.core:
Support is moving out of you and arriving. You know how to hold something up, and right now that's being used — a call answered, a weight taken off someone, a thing arranged before anyone had to ask. None of it is being calculated. It's operating.

What's less clear is the direction. Two or three places want the next portion of you, and from inside the fog they look equally plausible. You don't need to see the whole road. Pick the heading that matches what you actually want to have happen there, and follow that one for a week. The others stay open. They just don't get fed this week.
1.sheetLine: Pick the heading your support takes, and hold it a week.

2.tense: You are bracing already for the cost of helping before help has been asked.
2.verb: share your strength where it is actually needed
2.place: in the fog where the next step is visible but the road is not
2.ask: When a need seems to be forming nearby, hold still one breath and ask whether carrying it is actually yours. Let the small case decide, and move from what is on the table.
2.core:
The reach out is real and it runs past the situation. You sense what a person will need before they've said it, and you're already moving — arranging, supplying, arriving early. From outside it reads as plenty. From inside, some scan hasn't fully powered down.
