The difficulty isn't the helping. It's deciding from the picture you've assembled rather than from what's actually on the table now. Some of what you bring isn't needed yet, and carrying it costs you quietly. Before the next act of help, pause for a single breath. Let what's here answer the question instead of what you've already imagined. Then move, either way.
2.sheetLine: You may be supplying the imagined need, not the one present.

3.tense: You used to be the one people came to, and that door is behind you now.
3.verb: share your strength where it is actually needed
3.place: in the fog where the next step is visible but the road is not
3.ask: Stay inside a commitment that still has weight through the friction it brings — no sorting the whole life, just that engagement — and see what your strength holds.
3.core:
Something has you holding back. Not hoarding — just not reaching. Help doesn't move out of you the way it once did, and offers that come your way don't get picked up. You're standing at a door you've already stepped past, and the fog doesn't help: when you can't tell what's solid, waiting becomes the whole posture.

You don't need the whole road to find out. Stay with a commitment that still has weight in it, even a small one, while it's difficult. That friction shows you what your strength is made of now. Waiting until you feel ready first would defeat the test; from here, readiness and engagement are the same move.
3.sheetLine: Staying with a commitment through friction shows what still holds.

4.tense: You are already steering the direction here, and calling it the circumstances.
4.verb: share your strength where it is actually needed
4.place: in the fog where the next step is visible but the road is not
4.ask: For three days, choose a heading on purpose and hold it, even if it feels arbitrary and nobody sees. Notice how the week changes when the direction comes from you.
4.core:
Look at what got arranged. Resources moved, people got covered, timing worked out. That wasn't the room doing it. Someone was steering — and it was you, though you've been telling it as what the situation required, as if the situation had preferences.

The blind spot is your own hand in where things have gone. For three days, pick a direction deliberately and keep to it, however small. You don't need a reason that would satisfy anyone. Notice what the week does when the heading came from you, instead of from whichever way things already leaned. The steering is what you're not seeing, not the outcome.
4.sheetLine: You set this direction, and you've been calling it the situation.

1.tense: You are here, and what you are building carries your own weight in it.
1.verb: sharing your strength with what needs it
1.place: where you become what you already are
1.ask: Name the one thing this year is for, then steer by it for a week — turn down one good offer pointing elsewhere. A few options get dropped; a line gets drawn.
1.core:
You give your strength outward where it's needed, and it comes from something settled rather than from proving. There's a version of this where the direction is named, and what you hand out follows it instead of scattering. That's how it looks when it's going well: strength moving out from a decided center, not from a hurry.

To keep it, choose one direction and hold it a week. Decide the heading from what you actually want rather than from what follows logically, then steer. One good thing pointing another way can be let go. Generosity in every direction arrives nowhere in particular; a chosen line keeps what you share from thinning out. Naming it costs a few options and buys a spine.
1.sheetLine: Strength moves outward easier when it knows its direction.

2.tense: You are bracing for a future you cannot write in yet, so you are writing it early.
2.verb: sharing your strength with what needs it
2.place: where you become what you already are
2.ask: When a small thing is owed and nobody is watching, settle it. No weighing, no announcement.
2.core:
You give more than the moment calls for, and you run the fairness math ahead of time — who will need what, who might be slighted, what you'll owe before anyone has asked. Tending it that far ahead reads as care. It has started to feel like a debt you carry on behalf of the ones near you, and they can sense the accounting even when you say nothing.

Go smaller than the worry. When something small is owed and no one can see it, settle it, and trust the private sense of what's right to decide the case instead of running it through the ledger. One act, no tally. The brace mostly isn't needed for what you're bracing against; the ground holds without it.
2.sheetLine: The fairness you keep pre-paying costs more than it settles.

3.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
3.verb: sharing your strength with what needs it
3.place: where you become what you already are
3.ask: Take the piece of what you care about that pushes back hardest, and work on it this week to find out what in you holds when the friction comes.
3.core:
You have held a lot for others, and you have held it from back where you started, as though the strength were borrowed and might be called in. You take the shape someone needs you in. Standing in the middle of your own life, the part where something is yours to become, you arrive late. What you hand out works. The one who hands it out stands further back than it looks.

Go at the hard part on purpose. Pick the piece of what you care about that pushes back hardest, work on it this week, and see what in you holds under the resistance. This isn't to get through it. Strength shared doesn't come out of nowhere; it comes out of someone standing where they stand. You'll find the ground by walking on it.
3.sheetLine: You're holding the door open from the side that's already shut.

4.tense: You are steering without your hand on the wheel and calling it instinct.
4.verb: sharing your strength with what needs it
4.place: where you become what you already are
4.ask: Pick the direction you want, not the reasonable one, and face it for three days without telling anyone.
4.core:
Good things have grown around you, and you'd say they happened by themselves. You moved toward the right people, the right work, the right moment to step back, and filed each one under circumstance, luck, or being a supportive person. The steering has your hand on it. You don't sign it, so none of it counts as yours, and the thing you're becoming stays slightly out of view.

Go back to wanting. Face one way for three days, pointing your small choices somewhere you chose rather than somewhere logic approved. No announcement, no plan, nobody told. You've been treating your direction as something that arrives; it's a sentence you already wrote and didn't claim. Walk it, and it's yours.
4.sheetLine: The direction is already yours. You just haven't signed it.

1.tense: Right now you can hold the whole shape of it and your strength moves out to the part that needs it.
1.verb: move strength outward to where it is needed
1.place: in the whole pattern, seen from a step back
1.ask: Take the one heading the whole picture points toward, chosen from what you want rather than what seems logical, and hold it without looking around again.
1.core:
You can stand back and see how all of it fits, and your strength goes out to the part that is short. You do it without making a show of it; the help lands and whoever is on the other end can stand up on their own. Quiet holding of that kind is a real thing you can do, and there is nothing wrong with it.

The bend shows up when the shape keeps opening. You keep scanning, so what you hand over gets scattered thin across every gap at once. Take one heading, from what you want rather than what seems logical, and stay on it while the other needs wait at the edge. A set direction steadies where the support goes, and the part that matters gets all of what you have.
1.sheetLine: You see the whole and your strength goes where it's needed.

2.tense: You will have the whole picture soon and the help is already out of your hands before it is asked for.
2.verb: move strength outward to where it is needed
2.place: in the whole pattern, seen from a step back
2.ask: Set something right this week in a way nobody will notice, then forget you were the one who did it.
2.core:
You read the whole pattern and you read the people inside it, so your strength goes out before a request arrives. You have already worked out who is short and what you will hand them, and none of it has happened yet. Held that hard, support starts to press on people instead of keeping them up.

There is a quieter sense of what is fair in you, under the planning. Give it a case no one is watching: a wrong set right, unannounced, nobody answering. Fair exchange needs the other side to move too, and doing it unseen is how the count stays honest without you running it from the front. When nothing is weighing each gift, help stops landing before the need is there.
2.sheetLine: You're giving the help before the need has arrived.

3.tense: You were the one who saw the whole pattern, and you have stepped back from where the strength goes out.
3.verb: move strength outward to where it is needed
3.place: in the whole pattern, seen from a step back
3.ask: Go straight at the hard part you keep putting off and find out what still stands.
3.core:
You can read the whole shape of something and know where the strength belongs, and just now you are watching from the far side of the room. The help that used to move has stopped moving, and the quiet is noticeable to anyone near it. What you see stays seen and does not get handed anywhere.

Nothing here is broken. Take one hard part on purpose, the piece you keep putting off, and see what your commitment is actually made of. The wrong part falls away, the part that is yours holds, and either answer tells you something. Strength moves again once you have something to point it at.
3.sheetLine: You can see what's needed and you've stopped moving it.

4.tense: The strength is already moving outward through your hands and you are not counting it as yours.
4.verb: move strength outward to where it is needed
4.place: in the whole pattern, seen from a step back
4.ask: Give yourself a heading that isn't somebody's need, and steer by it where it won't show.
4.core:
Things hold around you. You see the whole pattern and strength keeps moving out to whoever needs it, and if someone asked what you did, it would come out as nothing much. The one keeping it all up is the one person you do not credit. This is yours; you just stopped being the one who gets to claim it.

There is a direction in you that answers no one else. Choose it on purpose, something you are building because you want it, and steer by that heading. Not instead of the support, underneath it. When the direction belongs to you rather than to the needs nearby, what goes outward has a source that knows itself, and strength stops draining out of an account nobody keeps.
4.sheetLine: The strength is yours, and you're not counting it as yours.

1.tense: You are here with the pen, and the strength you carry is moving outward by measure.
1.verb: sharing your strength outward by measure
1.place: the doorway where a thing is finished and can be let go
1.ask: Before the week fills, name the direction you want your strength to serve, in one sentence. Then give the week to that, not to whoever calls loudest.
1.core:
You share your strength outward, and you do it by measure — not everything at once, not to every open hand, the right amount to the right place. What you carry lands where it's needed, and things around you are steadier because of it.

Where this can still grow is direction. The sharing tends to follow whoever asks, which leaves the heading set by the asking rather than by you. Before the week fills, name the direction you want your strength to serve, say it in a sentence, and give the week to that — not to whoever calls loudest. What you want is a fair thing to steer by. Set the heading, and what you share has somewhere to go.
1.sheetLine: Name the direction your strength is for before the week fills.

2.tense: You are bracing toward a future you keep trying to write in advance, and every hand is out.
2.verb: sharing your strength outward by measure
2.place: the doorway where a thing is finished and can be let go
2.ask: Look at the three things you're holding up right now. Find the one where your honest sense says the arrangement is off, and act on that one — say the true thing, or move one piece — before anyone asks.
2.core:
The measure has slipped. You're trying to stand under a future you can't see yet, and every hand out looks like a hand that will empty unless you fill it. So the strength goes everywhere at once, not chosen for anything — and the weight you're under wasn't yours to hold in the first place.

You do have a private sense of what's fair in this. Use it. Look at the three things you're holding up right now, find the one where that sense says the arrangement is off, and act on that one — say the true thing, or move one piece — before anyone asks. The repair isn't giving less. It's giving from your own compass instead of from the pull.
2.sheetLine: You're holding up a future and every hand out looks like a bill.

3.tense: You are standing at a door that has already shut, and no hand is moving toward it.
3.verb: sharing your strength outward by measure
3.place: the doorway where a thing is finished and can be let go
3.ask: Take something you finished and didn't call finished. Do the rough piece once — hand over the last part, close the account, say the closing word — and see what holds after.
3.core:
You have strength. That isn't in question. What isn't happening is the sharing. The door is right there, a finished thing ready to leave your hands, and nothing reaches across it. Maybe there is nothing to hand out just now; maybe the outward face has gone quiet. Either way the strength sits with nowhere to go, and finishing has started to look like losing.

Trying harder won't do it. Take something you finished and didn't call finished — a handoff, an account, a word — and do the rough piece once: hand it over, close it, say it. What holds afterward will tell you what you've been staying on this side of the door for.
3.sheetLine: You won't walk through a door you already shut.

4.tense: You are steering with the pen down, and your account has someone else writing it.
4.verb: sharing your strength outward by measure
4.place: the doorway where a thing is finished and can be let go
4.ask: Name the want you had first, before it belonged to anyone else. Give the next stretch to it, with every other road left where it is.
4.core:
You have been the one steering for some time. The direction things took ran through your hands — wanting it, fixing on it, staying with it. Your telling has it as current, the way things went, with no steerer named. The people downstream have no reason to argue.

Before you were steering for those around you, you were someone with a light worth following. No need to summon every earlier version to reclaim that. Name the want you had first, before it belonged to anyone else, and give the next stretch to that alone, with every other road left where it is. Then the direction carries your name again.
4.sheetLine: You set the direction and call it current.
